UNIT-I.question: Explain the program development cycle.
UNIT-I.answer:
The program development cycle is a systematic process used to create reliable software. It includes several steps such as problem definition, design, coding, testing, debugging, and maintenance.

In the problem definition stage, the programmer understands requirements and objectives. During design, algorithms and flowcharts are prepared. Coding converts design into a program using a programming language such as Python.

Testing verifies correctness, while debugging removes errors. Maintenance ensures the program remains useful over time. Following this cycle improves quality and reduces mistakes.

UNIT-I.question: Explain variables, input, output and operators in Python.
UNIT-I.answer:
Variables in Python are used to store data values. They are created when assigned. Python supports numeric, string, and boolean types. Input is taken using input() function, while output is displayed using print().

Operators perform computations. Arithmetic operators include addition and subtraction. Comparison operators check relations, and logical operators combine conditions.

These elements form the foundation of Python programming.

UNIT-I.question: Explain decision and repetition structures.
UNIT-I.answer:
Decision structures allow execution of statements based on conditions. Python uses if, if-else, and if-elif-else. Nested decisions are also possible.

Repetition structures include while and for loops. They repeat instructions until conditions are met. Loops are essential for automation and calculations.

UNIT-II.question: Explain strings in Python.
UNIT-II.answer:
Strings are sequences of characters. They are used for text processing. Python allows accessing individual characters using indexing and slicing.

String methods such as upper, lower, replace, and split help manipulate text. Strings are immutable, meaning they cannot be changed after creation.

UNIT-II.question: Explain text file handling.
UNIT-II.answer:
Text files store information permanently. Python uses open() function to access files. Modes include read, write, and append.

Files are closed using close() to release resources. File handling is essential for applications involving data storage.

UNIT-II.question: Explain loops and control statements.
UNIT-II.answer:
Control statements guide program execution. for loop is used for definite iteration, while while loop works based on condition. Break and continue alter loop behavior.

They make programs flexible.

UNIT-III.question: Explain lists and dictionaries.
UNIT-III.answer:
Lists are ordered collections of elements. They are mutable and allow indexing. Methods such as append and remove are used to modify lists.

Dictionaries store data in key-value pairs. They allow fast retrieval. These structures are widely used in data processing.

UNIT-III.question: Explain functions and top-down design.
UNIT-III.answer:
Functions are reusable blocks of code. They reduce duplication and improve readability. Top-down design divides complex problems into smaller tasks implemented as functions.

This approach simplifies development and testing.

UNIT-III.question: Explain modules and packages.
UNIT-III.answer:
Modules are files containing Python code. They promote reuse. Packages are collections of modules organized in directories.

Using modules makes large programs manageable.

UNIT-IV.question: Explain file operations in Python.
UNIT-IV.answer:
Python provides several functions for file operations. read() reads entire file, readline() reads one line, and readlines() returns list of lines. Writing is done using write() and writelines().

seek() moves file pointer. These operations help in managing stored information.

UNIT-IV.question: Explain object oriented programming in Python.
UNIT-IV.answer:
Object oriented programming organizes software using classes and objects. A class defines properties and behaviors, while objects are instances. Constructors initialize data.

Inheritance allows reuse, and polymorphism enables flexibility. OOP improves modularity and maintainability.

UNIT-IV.question: Explain inheritance and polymorphism.
UNIT-IV.answer:
Inheritance allows new classes to acquire properties of existing ones. Polymorphism enables same function name to behave differently.

These features support extensibility.

UNIT-V.question: Explain exceptions in Python.
UNIT-V.answer:
Exceptions are errors that occur during execution. Python handles them using try, except, else, and finally blocks. Handling exceptions prevents program crash and ensures graceful recovery.

Users can also define custom exceptions.

UNIT-V.question: Explain graphical user interfaces.
UNIT-V.answer:
GUI programs allow users to interact visually through windows, buttons, and menus. Libraries such as Tkinter help create interfaces.

GUI improves usability compared to command-line programs.

UNIT-V.question: Explain Scratch programming.
UNIT-V.answer:
Scratch is a visual programming language designed for beginners. It uses blocks instead of text. It helps understand logic, loops, and events easily.

It is useful for learning programming fundamentals.
